key_insight: A blend of 50 wt.% chamotte, 25 wt.% bakor, and 25 wt.% corundum was selected for plasma-assisted formation of a stable glass-crystalline protective coating on chamotte refractories.
engineering_relevance: The approach targets stronger adhesion and greater thermal resistance in refractory linings for metallurgy, power generation, and chemical processing.
method: Select the blend using phase diagrams and melting curves for alumina–silica and alumina–silica–zirconia systems.
Mill powders to 80–100 µm, mix with sodium silicate binder, apply an approximately 1 mm layer, and dry.
Treat with concentrated low-temperature plasma; assess phase evolution and adhesion under thermal cycling.
evidence_signal: Evaluation included X-ray diffraction during 10 heating cycles to 1200 °C with air cooling and adhesion testing before and after cycling, but the abstract reports no numerical performance gains.
watch_item: Initial firebrick quality is critical to successful coating formation and may limit consistency in industrial implementation.
paper_title: Plasma Treatment Effect on Structure and Properties of Protective Coatings for Chamotte Refractories
